newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices mixed amid German worries.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices mixed amid German worries.

text.p: Danish bond prices were mixed on Thursday in a market made nervous by a row between the German government and the Bundesbank over government plans to revalue national gold reserves.
At 1300 GMT the benchmark eight percent Danish state bond due 2006 stood at 110.30 point -- yielding 6.42 percent -- up 0.04 point from Wednesday's close, but unchanged from early morning levels.
The seven percent state bond due 2007 traded at 102.82, yielding 6.60 percent, up from the morning's 102.77 but down from yesterday's 102.95.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund stood at 47 basis points, from Thursday's 48 bp and the 2007-bund gap narrowed by two basis points to 65 bp.
Turnover in the 2006 was about 1.6 billion crowns and in the 2007 it was around 275 million, dealers said.
The 2006 bond's June future rose 0.08 point, to 110.22, with 400 contracts traded.
The crown weakened to 3.8092 to the mark, from Wednesday's 3.8090. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.05 point to 88.70. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
